info.title: Gateward API
info.description: Multi-tenant identity provider — core auth, admin, API keys, and event querying.

get.summary:
ARCH-001: JWKS endpoint publishing the public keys of all active
signing key pairs. Unauthenticated — this is public key material
that any token verifier needs to validate signatures.
get.description:
ARCH-002: Cache-Control header tells clients/CDNs to cache the JWKS
for 1 hour (keys rotate on a much slower cadence — days/weeks, not
minutes). `public` allows shared caches; `max-age=3600` bounds it.

get.summary: Platform admin event query — no app_id scoping, all events visible.

delete.summary:
OPS-001: admin can revoke any session, not just their own. The
actor_id is logged so the audit trail records who revoked it.

patch.summary:
OPS-001 / AUDIT-STATUS-001: block, ban, or reactivate a user. `blocked`
(temporary) and `banned` (permanent) require a `reason` (§13.4) and
proactively revoke all active sessions — the access token TTL is 15 min,
so this is the difference between "eventual" and "immediate" enforcement
(CORE-006). Does NOT touch `locked_until` (the lockout system's field).

400.description: Invalid status, or missing reason for block/ban

patch.summary:
Operator annotations at the identity level — set from the dashboard when
someone investigates a user and wants to record notes/tags/behavior.
Distinct from the per-app `local_metadata` an app writes about its own user.

400.description: metadata must be a JSON object

post.summary:
Plan V6 §11.1/§13.2: identical response whether or not the email
exists in this identity_pool.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user belongs to

202.description: Reset email sent (or email doesn't exist)

post.summary:
Plan V6 §4.1/§13.3. Order matters for anti-enumeration: password and
membership are checked before account_status is ever allowed to
affect the response, so blocked/banned/locked never leak beyond the
same generic error as a bad password.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user is logging into

post.summary:
Plan V6 §7.13: platform admins live in the system identity_pool and
aren't scoped to any app, so this is a dedicated login path rather
than the app-scoped /v1/auth/login (CORE-001).

Plan V6 §13.1: always the same response shape whether the email was
new or already existed in this identity_pool — no session/tokens
either way, login happens as a separate call.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user is registering into

post.summary:
Plan V6 §12/§13: identical response whether the email doesn't exist,
is already verified, or genuinely got a new token — never reveals
which case applies.

parameters.name: X-Gateward-App-Id
parameters.description: App ID the user belongs to

post.summary:
Plan V6 §11.2/§11.3: revokes every active session for the user
within its identity_pool once the password changes. No AppContext
needed — token possession is the authorization, and the token
already carries its own ecosystem/pool/app.
Plan V6 §12. No AppContext needed — same reasoning as reset_password.

get.summary:
AUTHZ-002: app-scoped event query. Service accounts with
`events:read_app` see only their own app's events. Platform admins
get the full view. If a non-admin passes an app_id filter, it must
match their token's app_id (cross-app enforcement).

200.description: List of events (scoped to caller's app for service accounts)

403.description: Missing events:read_app scope or not platform admin

post.summary:
Plan V6 §18.1 `sendEvent`. Service accounts with `events:write` emit
custom app events. The ecosystem/pool/app are taken from the caller's
credential — never the body — so an app can only write into its own
scope (cross-app safe). `event_type` must be namespaced (contain a
`.`), which keeps app events from colliding with the Core's internal
snake_case audit events (§11.2/§15) — none of which contain a `.`.

404.description: Session not found or not owned
No membership in the caller's app

400.description: metadata must be a JSON object

404.description: No membership in the caller's app

Jwk.description:
JWK as published in the JWKS endpoint. RFC 7517 §4.
`crv = "P-256"`, `kty = "EC"`, `alg = "ES256"` for ES256 keys.

metadata.description: JSON object shallow-merged into the membership's `local_metadata`.

event_type.description:
Namespaced event type, e.g. `app.checkout.completed`. Must contain
a `.` and use `[a-z0-9._-]` only.

metadata.description: Arbitrary JSON object with event details.

user_id.description:
Optional user this event is about. If set, must belong to the
caller's identity pool.

reason.description:
Required when blocking/banning (Plan V6 §13.4). Stored on the user and
recorded in the event; cleared when reactivating.

status_reason.description: Why the account is blocked/banned (AUDIT-STATUS-001). Null when active.
